findings.observation: The complete axe remains visible, but the crown and upper blade reach to roughly 7% from the top edge, crossing the required 8% safe margin.
Exactly one complete axe is present with no duplicate weapon, detached component, or extra gear.
The single-edged bearded blade, eye and poll, short haft, wrapped grip, and capped butt read immediately as a one-hand bearded axe.
The eye, cheek, visible pin, shouldered haft, wraps, and butt cap form coherent construction, but the unusually broad blacksteel head raises a practical one-hand weight and balance concern.
Blacksteel dominates the large head and remains the sole rank-bearing focal material; the worn wood haft and dark wraps are neutral and subordinate.
Dense hammered texture, dark oxidized recesses, rubbed bright bevels, and narrow cold reflections establish blacksteel through physical surface response beyond palette alone.
There is no supernatural emission or full-object glow; rank behavior stays bounded to controlled blacksteel reflectance and a narrow warm rim.
Premium realistic painterly rendering, honest wear, cold key light, restrained warm rim, midnight-charcoal ground, and subtle floor plane follow the accepted profile.
All declared negative constraints are visually satisfied except no-oversized-silhouettes: the exceptionally broad head is oversized relative to the short one-hand haft and requested practical role.
